h: Praise and Confession Open the Gates of Shabbos Holiness

p: of the Field of apples, etc."
"Open for me the gates of righteousness (tzedek)";
"I will enter through them and thank God"
that one can come to this
And this is "I will sing in praises
which is the attribute of Malchus,
And so they are called the gates of Gan Eden,
the aspect of the Field of apples;
And this is what they answered
about the gates of Gan Eden
that only the righteous shall enter
And in the future each one will be refined
(כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב רֵישׁ חֵלֶק, סַנְהֶדְרִין צ, א)
(as is written at the beginning of Perek Chelek, Sanhedrin 90a).
that a righteous nation that keeps faith may enter"
regarding one who answers "Amen" with all his strength,
that the gates of Gan Eden are opened for him.
And that is from what is written,
the gates are the gates of righteousness,
which corresponds to the attribute of Malchus,
(and it was explained in Parshas Mishpatim).
וְהַשִּׁיר שֶׁל שַׁבָּת מַתְחִיל (תְּהִלִּים צב, ב)
And the song of Shabbos begins (Tehillim 92:2):
"It is good to give thanks to Hashem
and to sing to Your Name, O Most High";
for on Shabbos there is a revelation
that is, Yisrael are bound at the root,
at the beginning of the Thought;
for Shabbos is a time of teshuvah,
וּכְמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב (בְּרֵאשִׁית רַבָּה סוֹף פָּרָשָׁה כב)
as is written (Bereishis Rabbah, end of chapter 22):
"So great is the power of teshuvah,
and said, 'A psalm, a song for the day of Shabbos'";
and it is written, "It is good to give thanks (lehodos) to Hashem."
וְאִיתָא עַל זֶה בְּפִרְקֵי דְּרַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר
And it is found about this in Pirkei d'Rabbi Eliezer,
"One who confesses (modeh) and forsakes will be shown mercy."
And although there it is written "confesses and forsakes,"
while here it is written "It is good to give thanks,"
and he forsakes the evil of himself;
similar to what is found in the Pesikta (for Shabbos Shuvah):
and exchanges it for a light thing;
and what is the light thing?
קְחוּ עִמָּכֶם דְּבָרִים (הוֹשֵׁעַ יד, ג) וְכוּלֵּי
וְהוּא עַל דֶּרֶךְ שֶׁאָמַר (תַּעֲנִית ח, א)
And it is along the lines of what is said (Taanis 8a):
"'And they beguiled Him with their mouth, etc.' (Tehillim 78:36),
וְהוּא רַחוּם יְכַפֵּר עָוֹן (תְּהִלִּים עח, לח)
which corresponds to the attribute of Malchus
we call it the Oral Torah"
"My words that I have put in your mouth";
as is found in Sefer Yetzirah
that Shabbos was created in the year
and the mouth in the soul.
only that then the power was created in the mouth,
and it be in the aspect of the mouth of Hashem,
"My words that I have put in your mouth";
וּכְמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב בַּזּוֹהַר הַקָּדוֹשׁ (חֵלֶק ג רא, ב)
and as is written in the holy Zohar (III 201b):
וּכְמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב בַּזּוֹהַר הַקָּדוֹשׁ (חֵלֶק א לב, א)
And as is written in the holy Zohar (I 32a):
That is, that a person speaks
and it is in the aspect of the mouth of Hashem;
and about this it is written (Yeshayahu 55:11):
כֵּן יִהְיֶה דְבָרִי אֲשֶׁר יֵצֵא מִפִּי
"So shall be My word that goes forth from My mouth:
it shall not return to Me empty,
and it is the aspect of the mouth of Hashem,
"and his heart will understand, and he will repent."
And because of this it is written:
"It is good to give thanks to Hashem";
he will merit that it enter the heart,
and he will be one who "confesses and forsakes,"
and he will be included in
so that he can enter the gates of righteousness,
the gate that the righteous enter.
And therefore King David, peace be upon him,
who was a chariot for the attribute of Malchus
that he sated the Holy One, blessed be He,
and this is "I will enter through them and thank God";
for such is the way of one who comes before the king,
to say songs and praises before him.
And so it is found in the Zohar Chadash (Bereishis 19):
He created angels and holy Chayos,
the heavens and all their host,
to praise their Creator and glorify Him;
yet there was still no praise before Him
and burst forth in song and praise,
the upper and lower ones, etc."
And this is why they instituted
in the blessing before Krias Shema of Shabbos:
and sat upon His throne of glory, etc."
that then they recognized the glory of His kingship,
for this is the attribute of Shabbos,
"and the seventh day praises and says, etc.;
therefore let all His creatures glorify and bless God,
all the creatures did not say song
until the day of Shabbos came,
of which it is written, "It is good to give thanks to Hashem,"
and then they all opened and said song.
And this is "I will sing in praises
which is the attribute of Malchus,
"I will enter through them and thank God."
